observation_summary: FastDateFormat produces an incorrect week-of-year value when formatting dates because it fails to use the locale-specific settings (firstDayOfWeek and minimalDaysInFirstWeek) provided during instance creation, defaulting to system locale settings instead.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic failure in the date formatting logic. The component is supposed to respect the provided locale's calendar rules for calculating the week number, but it incorrectly uses the system's default calendar settings. This is a procedural error in how the date-to-week calculation is performed, requiring a correction to the internal logic that initializes or uses the Calendar instance for formatting.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'FastDateFormat apparently doesn't respect the locale it was sent on creation when outputting week in year... It seems to use the settings of the system locale for firstDayOfWeek and minimalDaysInFirstWeek'
The failing test shows a discrepancy in the calculated week number (53 vs 01) for the same date and locale.
The issue is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple wrong constant (Assignment/Initialization), but a failure in the computational procedure to correctly apply locale-specific calendar rules.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve initializing a Calendar object with specific locale settings, the root cause is the procedural failure to correctly derive the week number based on the provided locale, which is an algorithmic/methodological flaw.
The capability to format dates exists; the implementation of the week-of-year calculation is simply incorrect, not missing.
